references.text: Prohibition against eating meat from animals torn to death by wild beasts. The same term 'טְרֵפָה' (torn) is used in both places.
Laws concerning uncleanness through touching a carcass (נְבֵלָה). Whoever eats of a dead animal becomes unclean.
Regulations regarding one who eats a dead or torn animal. Must wash and remains unclean until evening.
Prohibition against eating animals that died naturally because Israel is a holy people to the Lord.
Ezekiel declares that he has never eaten meat from an animal that died naturally or was torn, using the same Hebrew words 'נְבֵלָה וּטְרֵפָה'.
The priests shall not eat anything that died naturally or was torn. The same prohibition is repeated for the priesthood in the future temple.
